subject: Edgeware MSA / Order Form — defense control trigger & evidence staging
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edgeware redlines — IP indemnity and evidence handoff (MSA + OF)

Kimberly / Grace —

Quick background: Edgeware (security-focused analytics) pushed a relatively aggressive set of MSA redlines during legal review. Their key asks are: defense control for any third-party IP claim that "arises from the use of the Services," a broad evidence-collection cooperation clause, and expedited notice/response timelines. Procurement is asking us to take a position so they can finalize the order form.

I've attached their redline (Edgeware_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and a diff of the order form. Highlights for legal:
- They want defense control (their counsel insists on right to defend) for 3P claims tied to output/inference.
- They want us to preserve evidence (logs, model inputs) for 2 years and require a 5 business-day initial response SLA from us after notice.
- They also request a carveout for any claims arising from customer-provided data.

Customer contacts: Maria Lopez (legal lead) and procurement@edgeware.com. Sales asks: can we offer a hybrid (Redwood leads defense but customer can assume if they reimburse costs / agree to certain cooperation steps)? If we need exec approval for an exception to our default 'right to defend' position, let me know and I can run revenue/IC with Finance.

Thanks — want to get this closed before the next procurement window (they're aiming to sign by 07/10).

—Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edgeware redlines — IP indemnity and evidence handoff (MSA + OF)

Thanks Ben — reviewed initial redline. High-level legal position below. I put inline comments in the attached doc as well.

Summary of our preferred position:
- Maintain Right to Defend for third-party IP claims; we can offer a limited option to allow Customer to defend (only) if they: (a) provide a written undertaking to indemnify Redwood for additional costs exceeding our insurance limits, and (b) use counsel reasonably acceptable to Redwood.
- Evidence preservation: agree to reasonable preservation of logs / KV cache snapshots for the notice window, but we will not agree to a blanket 2-year retention on the basis of special procurement. We can propose a 90-day hot retention + 18-month cold archive, subject to region/security constraints.
- Response SLA: 5 business days for acknowledgement is reasonable; 5 business days for substantive response is aggressive for legal/forensics — propose 10 business days for substantive reply with an initial triage confirm at 3 business days.

Open questions for Sales/CS:
1) Is Edgeware insisting on defense control as a dealbreaker, or is this negotiable? (Ben)
2) Are there particular outputs or customer-provided models/data that would meaningfully change risk allocation? (Grace)
3) Can we get procurement to accept the 90-day/18-month retention compromise?

Jonas — can you advise on whether the proposed option (customer may defend subject to indemnity for excess costs) is something we should escalate to Ops/Insurance? If so we need to run numbers.

I'll draft a concise counter to send to Maria that lays out our hybrid offer and the evidence retention compromise. If you can get me confirmation on deal sensitivity, I'll mirror the language to make it signable.

—Kimberly
Senior Counsel, IP & Tech Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Edgeware_MSA_redline_v3.docx (redline)

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@edgeware.com>

Cc: Edgeware Legal <legal@edgeware.com>, procurement@edgeware.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 14:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Edgeware redlines — IP indemnity and evidence handoff (MSA + OF)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick read. A few notes from our side:
- Defense control is important to us for any claim tied to output that impacts our customers. We have internal policies (and customer obligations) that make defense control the default.
- We are open to the hybrid defense model if Redwood provides concrete language that ensures timely cooperation and allows us to preserve our customer relationships while handling notices.
- On retention: Edgeware needs at least 18 months of searchable evidence for potential investigations — the 90-day hot + 18-month cold archive seems like a workable technical compromise if you can commit to the ability to export data on reasonable request.
- Regarding timelines: we can accept a 3 business day triage and a 10 business day substantive response. The 5 business day expectation for anything beyond acknowledgement is difficult for our legal ops as well.

I'll review your proposed counter once you send it. Procurement is pushing for signature in the July cycle but legal can be flexible if we converge this week.

Best,
Maria Lopez
General Counsel (acting)
Edgeware Inc

Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edgeware redlines — IP indemnity and evidence handoff (MSA + OF)

Couple of operational notes from Ops/Infra standpoint to include in counter:
- Evidence export: we can support on-demand exports for 18 months if Edgeware pays for egress/time-to-export in the order form (suggest line item: evidence retrieval fee or execution SLA).
- Log retention tiers: propose explicit language: "Hot logs (90 days, immediate access); Cold logs (18 months, export within 5 business days subject to retrieval fee)."
- For customer-provided data carveout: we will accept carveout for claims originating solely from customer data or models that were not processed by Redwood transformation/pipeline, but we need a representation/confirmation from customer in the OF about data origin.

From Insurance perspective (quick note): allowing customer control of defense without limits increases our tail-risk. If they insist, require an excess indemnity and that counsel meet minimum qualifications (no conflict, standard of counsel). I can help draft the escalation bullet for 1:1 with Insurance if Kimberly wants to push for that route.

Happy to take a pass at the counter language that threads Ops + Legal + Insurance constraints.

—Jonas
Director, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@edgeware.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jul 2025 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edgeware redlines — IP indemnity and evidence handoff (MSA + OF)

Maria / Team —

Thanks for the helpful clarification. Below is the counter we plan to send this afternoon if this aligns with Edgeware's flexibility:

1) Defense control: Redwood will retain the right to assume defense for third-party IP claims. Customer may elect to control defense only if Customer: (a) executes a written indemnity for amounts in excess of Redwood's insurance limits; (b) engages counsel reasonably acceptable to Redwood; and (c) provides immediate cooperation (preserve evidence; no admissions).

2) Evidence retention & export: Redwood will maintain hot logs for 90 days with immediate access and cold logs for 18 months accessible via export. Export will be provided within 5 business days subject to a standard evidence retrieval fee (to be quoted in the order form). Redwood will commit to providing a packaged export (logs + relevant KV snapshots) when requested by Edgeware's legal team under a valid notice.

3) Notice & response cadence: Redwood will provide triage acknowledgement within 3 business days and a substantive response within 10 business days. If legal or forensics requires additional time, Redwood will provide regular status updates.

4) Carveout for customer data: Redwood will not indemnify claims arising solely from customer-provided data or models. Customer should confirm data-origin in the Order Form representation section.

If this is acceptable, Ben — please route to procurement and Maria for final confirmation and we'll produce a short one-page amendment to the OF documenting the retrieval fee and the defense option language. If Edgeware needs Redwood to waive the "right to defend" outright, we'll need a formal Exception Request for approval from Legal + Insurance + Finance (likely escalates to a small executive review).

Maria — can you confirm by 07/03 EOD if Edgeware is willing to accept this compromise so we can lock the July signing window?

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, IP & Tech Contracts
Redwood Inference
